subject: Live chat response slowdown — mitigation summary & client runbook
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@greenline.com>, Greenline SRE <sre@greenline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Live chat response slowdown — mitigation steps we are applying

Hi Evan —

We observed elevated p95/p99 latency for your streaming chat endpoint (model: rwd-small-v1, region: us-west-2) starting ~08:50 PT and affecting message chunk delivery to clients. You may have seen partial or delayed chunks in your support widget and a few timeouts.

Summary of impact: short bursts of 1.5–3s extra per-chunk latency for ~10% of requests during the window; overall request success stayed >99%, but perceived responsiveness degraded for interactive sessions.

What we're doing (short term):
- Rolling a routing change to prefer warm dedicated instances for Greenline traffic for the next 2 hours.
- Temporarily decreasing the default streaming chunk size to 256 tokens for interactive sessions to reduce per-chunk processing.
- Enabling a fallback path: if stream handshake doesn't complete in 700ms, we will return the first non-streaming response to the client to avoid perceived freeze.

Actions for your team (recommended, optional):
- If you can, set client-side stream timeout to 900ms and implement a single-attempt non-stream fallback when you detect an incomplete stream.
- Reduce max_tokens on your user-facing prompts to 512 for the next 6 hours.
- If you rely on low-latency assistant typing events, enable progressive rendering of partial chunks (we can share sample code).

I'll follow up with an incident timeline and a short runbook for your ops team. We will also provide a telemetry snippet (attached) showing request-level latencies and trace IDs to map back to your logs.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand how important immediate responsiveness is for Greenline's support flows.

Best,
Olga
Account Lead, North America
Redwood Inference

Attachments: greenline-telemetry-snippet.txt (text), incident-timeline-20270322.pdf (placeholder)

From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@greenline.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenline SRE <sre@greenline.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 09:28:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Live chat response slowdown — mitigation steps we are applying

Thanks Olga — appreciate the quick heads-up. A couple quick Qs:

1) Can you confirm whether this routing change affects only Greenline traffic, or is it global? We want to understand potential cache/throughput tradeoffs.
2) Any risk of partial responses when you enable the 700ms non-stream fallback? We prefer no truncated assistant text if avoidable.

We can do the client-side timeout and reduce max_tokens — but want to avoid visible truncation for customers. If you think the non-stream fallback is safe (i.e., will return full final text rather than a partial chunk), confirm and we'll coordinate changes on our side.

Evan
Director, Platform Engineering
Greenline

On the telemetry: can you include the Trace IDs so our SREs can join the dots with our app logs?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@greenline.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 09:40:10 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Live chat response slowdown — mitigation steps we are applying

Olga / Ben —

Looping in Ben from Support Engineering for fallback behavior confirmation; I'm happy to own the routing rollback if we see customer impact rise.

Ben — quick notes from infra: the routing change pins Greenline requests to their warm pool (so it's Greenline-only), which should reduce queuing variance. The 700ms non-stream fallback will trigger a synchronous non-stream generation (same model, single-shot path) — it returns the completed text rather than a chunk; we tested for the most common prompt shapes and saw no truncation issues. If any customers rely on partially streamed token-by-token UX, they may see the first complete response arrive slightly later than the first chunk would have, but it prevents indefinite stalls.

Ben, please confirm the telemetry trace IDs are included in the attached snippet and whether we can extend retention for them for one week.

-Marissa
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@greenline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Greenline SRE <sre@greenline.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 15:12:03 -0700
Subject: RE: Live chat response slowdown — mitigation steps we are applying

Hi Evan — thanks for the quick replies and for coordinating on the client changes. Final update and next steps: 

What we found and fixed:
- Root cause: transient scheduler regression in the streaming worker pool in us-west-2 that produced uneven token-processing latency under certain prefix distributions.
- Fix applied: we deployed a scheduler patch at 11:04 PT that normalizes slice assignment to workers and reduces inter-token jitter.
- Observed result: p95/p99 latency returned to baseline within ~20 minutes after the patch; no data loss.

What we rolled back/kept on: 
- Routing change (pinning to warm instances) was removed at 11:45 PT after we confirmed stable latency.
- We left the 700ms non-stream fallback enabled for an additional 2 hours as a protective measure.

Customer-facing mitigations we recommend (summary you can follow):
1) Client-side stream timeout = 900ms + fallback to non-stream call. This avoids indefinite waiting and preserves complete responses.
2) Temporarily reduce max_tokens for interactive widgets to 512.
3) Implement progressive render of partial content where possible — we can provide a small JS snippet that reconstructs partial chunks safely.

Attached: incident-timeline-20270322.pdf (timeline), client-temporary-runbook.md (step-by-step config that your SREs can follow), plus greenline-telemetry-snippet.txt with Trace IDs (example IDs: trace-20270322-01b, trace-20270322-02f, trace-20270322-03a).

We will produce a full post-incident report (root cause + long-term mitigations and a regression test) by 2027-03-29. For immediate remediation, if you want us to toggle the 700ms fallback off earlier or keep it until midnight PST, say the word and we'll comply.

Separately, Marissa and I will follow up on a short credit offer for the minutes of degraded UX; we'll route that via your billing contact.

Sorry again for the disruption — appreciate your partnership and fast collaboration.

Best,
Olga
Account Lead, North America
Redwood Inference
